label: Almond Row: repeated reset_or_restart on central_inverter with declining benefit
headline: No efficacy decay at Almond Row — the pattern is one escalated work order across five different inverters with no measured benefit data, and matched work orders at four other sites show the same reset-and-resolve behaviour.
action: Close this candidate and instead pull the full 2025 fault and reset history plus firmware revision for the single unit KVP36-2419B-0371 to confirm or dismiss its stated second overtemperature recurrence.
reasoning: The 'declining benefit' rests on no measured benefit at all — benefit_pct is null on all five members (WO-2025-00308, WO-2025-00465, WO-2025-00638, WO-2025-00651, WO-2025-00847) — so the trend is one escalated/recurring outcome (WO-2025-00847) out of three late-window WOs, across five distinct asset IDs with no asset resetting twice inside the cluster. The matched controls settle it: WO-2025-00770 (Frostline Prairie) carries essentially the same undervoltage-reset-monitor-two-hours narrative as WO-2025-00465/WO-2025-00638, and WO-2026-00410 (Kernwood Basin) and WO-2024-00104 (Caprock Mesa) repeat the same overcurrent-trip/reset/no-pattern text as WO-2025-00308 — identical behaviour and outcomes at sites outside this cluster, so Almond Row is not distinguishable from the fleet. That also defeats H4: the text templating is corpus-wide, not an Almond Row reporting habit inflating this cluster. H2 fails because only two members (WO-2025-00651, WO-2025-00847) are thermal, on two different assets, both with intakes and heat sinks verified clear, and the control PMs show normal thermal margins (WO-2025-00618: 44 C cabinet at 36 C ambient). H3 rests on a single tech's uncertain aside about fw 4.2.1 in WO-2025-00847 with no second WO on that asset and three different symptom families across the members, which is exactly the pattern the hypothesis itself calls implausible for one software defect.
contradicting: WO-2025-00847 explicitly states it is the second overtemperature event this season on KVP36-2419B-0371 and was escalated, and the prior event is not present in this cluster — so at least one Almond Row inverter does have genuine recurrence that this five-WO view does not capture. The firmware note (fw 4.2.1) on that same unit is untested here because no asset-to-firmware join was provided.

population_detail.description: No systemic population established; the five members are five distinct central inverters with no shared defect signature demonstrated.

hypotheses.statement: There is no real efficacy decay: the 'decline' is one escalated work order out of three in the late window (1/3 = 0.33) spread across five distinct asset IDs, i.e. ordinary small-sample variation with no repeated reset on any single inverter.
predictions: All five member WOs carry different asset_id values (KVP36-2405A-0104, 2421B-0201, 2408A-0124, 2435C-0234, 2419B-0371) — only one asset (…0371) has any recurrence flag, and even that recurrence is not represented by a second WO in the cluster.
mean_benefit_early_pct, mean_benefit_late_pct and benefit_drop_pct are all null, so the 'declining benefit' label rests entirely on outcome codes, not on any measured benefit.
Other site|action|component combinations of similar n (~5) in the corpus should show comparable early/late ineffective-share swings of 0.0→0.25–0.50 purely from one non-resolved WO.
Reclassifying the cluster per-asset yields five clusters of n=1 and no efficacy trend at all.
discriminating_evidence: Pull the full reset history per inverter serial: if any single asset has ≥3 resets with lengthening recurrence, H1 is weakened and H3 strengthened.
Bootstrap the late-ineffective share over all clusters with n≤6 at this site; if 0.33 sits inside the central 80% of that null distribution, the candidate is noise.

hypotheses.statement: The late-window failures are seasonal: overtemperature trips on central inverters concentrate in July–September peak ambient, so reset efficacy falls in summer for thermal reasons and will recover in autumn without any hardware change.
predictions: Symptom mix shifts by date within the cluster: overcurrent/undervoltage in April–May, overtemperature in July and September — which is exactly what the five members show.
Site-wide, overtemperature_trip WO counts on central_inverter at Almond Row should peak in the same July–September months across all actions, not just reset_or_restart.
Other sites in the corpus in the same climate window should show a parallel summer rise in overtemperature_trip WOs on central inverters.
Post-September WOs at Almond Row should revert to non-thermal symptoms and 0% ineffective resets.
discriminating_evidence: Compare the monthly overtemperature WO rate at Almond Row against other sites: a site-specific summer excess points away from pure seasonality toward cooling/derate design; a common seasonal shape supports H2.
Check whether narratives report cleared intakes/filters (they do here, twice) — clean cooling paths plus summer timing favours ambient-driven trips over fouling-driven wear.

hypotheses.statement: A firmware/configuration defect on a subset of Almond Row central inverters (e.g. build 4.2.1 noted in WO-2025-00847) produces spurious protection trips that a reset only clears temporarily, so recurrence grows on the affected units.
predictions: Asset-level records should show that the trip-affected inverters share a firmware revision or configuration flag, while non-tripping units at the same site differ.
The escalated WO (WO-2025-00847) should be followed within weeks by a firmware-update or vendor-support WO on the same or sibling assets.
NO-FAULT-FOUND / RESET resolution codes with empty parts_used should be over-represented at Almond Row versus other sites for central_inverter CM work — consistent with nothing physical being wrong.
After any firmware remediation WO, subsequent reset-type WOs on those assets should drop to near zero.
discriminating_evidence: Join firmware revision to asset_id for all five members: if all five share 4.2.1 and non-member inverters do not, H3 rises sharply above H1/H2.
If the trips span multiple distinct firmware revisions and multiple symptom families (overcurrent, undervoltage, overtemp), a single software defect is implausible.

hypotheses.statement: Narrative text is being cloned between work orders (WO-2025-00465 and WO-2025-00638 are near-identical except for the asset ID and a trailing clause), so the extracted symptom/action/outcome fields are partly duplicated template content rather than independent observations.
predictions: String-similarity scoring across the corpus should flag other WO pairs at Almond Row with >0.9 narrative overlap, disproportionately from the same tech (TECH-0124 authored both duplicates here).
Duplicated narratives should co-occur with null benefit_pct and heterogeneous labor_hours (5.9 h vs 1.6 h for identical text), indicating the text was not written from the actual visit.
Per-tech ineffective/recurring rates should differ materially: TECH-0051 authored both 'uncertain' or recurring-flagged narratives in this cluster.
Removing duplicate-text WOs should collapse the cluster below the minimum member threshold.
discriminating_evidence: Compare SCADA/meter downtime timestamps against each WO's claimed monitoring window: if the two identical narratives correspond to genuinely different fault events, cloning is cosmetic and the cluster's counts survive; if one has no matching event, the member count is inflated.
Check whether the 37.5 MWh lost-energy total is entered per-WO or back-filled uniformly — uniform values would confirm template/default population rather than measurement.
